Figure 1:From planner to agent for history-dependent manipulation.Top: Similar observations can require different decisions depending on task progress.
(a) Memory-augmented policies equip VLA models with memory mechanisms to retain and use
historical information. (b) Hierarchical planning separates high-level planning from
low-level execution. (c) SERA uses an editable harness to organize the VLM as an agent that maintains
task context from observation and interaction history. Execution-driven self-evolution
refines the harness using rollout feedback. The dashed arrow denotes the selected
harness, fixed before testing.

Figure 2:Agentic execution and harness self-evolution.(a)The harness maintains task context and uses a VLM to plan commands
for a VLA executor, incorporating execution feedback in subsequent rounds.(b)Execution traces guide revisions to planning guidance, assessment
criteria, and control rules. A verifier evaluates candidates and informs further
revision and selection; the selected harness is fixed before testing.
Tokens denote information categories and image stacks show observation sequences.

Figure 3:Self-evolution results and complementary execution cases.(a) RoboMME success rates before and after harness revision.
(b) VideoPlaceOrder: the base agent analyzes a demonstration to identify
the intended target despite a swap, then uses retained task context to
predict its current location and successfully place the cube.
(c) PatternLock: self-evolution diagnoses direction-mapping errors and
missing action candidates, revises the direction guidance and candidate
set, and the revised agent successfully completes the sequence.
VideoPlaceOrder shows a test episode; PatternLock shows a self-evolution repair example.
Direction guides and candidate colors are schematic; paths show
motion and target order.
